EAQ31.brief: Movie Render Queue, often shortened to MRQ, is the tool in Unreal for rendering final images and videos. It can spend more time on each frame than the viewport does, so the result is cleaner than a normal screenshot. It renders from a Level Sequence, which is the asset Unreal uses for cinematics. In this quest you render one frame with Movie Render Queue and compare it with a High Resolution Screenshot.
checklist: Create a Level Sequence that is one frame long and uses your Cine Camera.
Render it with Movie Render Queue. Use anti-aliasing samples, which smooth jagged edges by rendering the frame several times, and choose a high resolution.
Save the render settings as a preset, so that you can use them again later.
Take a High Resolution Screenshot of the same frame and compare it with the render.
EAQ31.done_when: Send the MRQ still, the viewport screenshot, and a screenshot of your preset.

EAQ35.brief: A reference scene is a neutral level with known lighting that people use to check their assets. When everyone on the server puts an asset into the same scene, everyone judges it under the same light, so the results can be compared. In this quest you build such a scene with what you learned in the earlier quests, write a short guide for it, and show it to a mentor.
checklist: Build a scene that other members can drop assets into to check them. Include neutral props, a pair of balls (one gray and one chrome), and a Macbeth-style swatch board, which is a board of standard color patches.
Light the scene with physical units and give it a hero area (from quest EAQ29). Use a fixed exposure.
Use your master material, one material function, and one vertex-painted blend (from quests EAQ25, EAQ26 and EAQ27).
Provide 3 Cine Cameras that are saved as bookmarks, and an MRQ preset (from quest EAQ31).
Write a README of one page. It must say how to use the scene, what the exposure is, and what people should not change.
Walk a mentor through the scene, either live or in a recorded clip.
EAQ35.done_when: Send your scene and README to a mentor. The mentor signs off after opening the scene and checking one asset in it using only your README.

EAQ32.brief: PCG means Procedural Content Generation. It is a system in Unreal where you build a graph of rules, and the graph places many objects for you. Set dressing is the work of filling a scene with small objects such as rocks and debris, and PCG makes this much faster than placing each one by hand. In this quest you scatter objects on a surface with a PCG graph and add a rule that keeps the paths free.
checklist: Make a PCG graph that scatters debris or rocks on a surface.
Add one rule to the graph that keeps the paths clear. It can be a density rule, which controls how many objects appear, or an exclusion rule, which removes objects from an area.
EAQ32.done_when: Send a screenshot of the scattered objects, and also a screenshot of the graph.

EAQ33.brief: The Water system is a plugin in Unreal that gives you ready-made lakes, rivers and oceans. Water reflects everything around it, so its color and clarity have a strong effect on the mood of a scene. In this quest you add a small water body and adjust it until it fits your mood target.
checklist: Add a small lake or a river to your scene with the Water system.
Tune the color and the scattering of the water until it matches your mood target. Scattering controls how light spreads inside the water, which changes how clear or murky it looks.
EAQ33.done_when: Send a still image of the water in your scene.

EAQ34.brief: A Procedural Foliage Volume is a box that fills an area with trees and plants by simulating how they spread. You give it foliage types, which act like species, each with its own spacing rules. Plants with the same distance between them look artificial, so the settings matter. In this quest you set up a volume with two species and tune it until the edge of the forest looks natural.
checklist: Set up a Procedural Foliage Volume with 2 species.
Tune the spacing settings until the edge of the forest looks natural and not uniform.
EAQ34.done_when: Send a screenshot of the forest edge.
